newsitem.title: USA: Tip from first lady leads to doctor arrest.
newsitem.headline: Tip from first lady leads to doctor arrest.

text.p: Acting on a tip that came through first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, authorities Thursday accused a New York doctor of stealing more than $1 million from Medicare and Medicaid.
One of the doctor's patients wrote a letter to the first lady voicing suspicions about his billing practices and state authorities were alerted, said New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco.
Dr. Jeffrey Schwartz, 41, of Atlantic Beach, a New York City suburb, allegedly billed Medicare and Medicaid for more than 13,000 medical procedures and tests he never performed.
Many of his patients were elderly, and eight of them were dead when he claimed to have performed the procedures, Vacco said.
Forty-seven other patients were in hospitals where Schwartz did not practice, Vacco said. The fraud occured between 1989 and 1995, he said.
Schwartz had a private office and also treated patients at four nursing homes in New York's Long Island region.
"Schwartz deliberately targeted elderly nursing home patients, using their infirmities to steal from taxpayers to line his own pockets," Vacco said.
The unidentified patient told Clinton she had looked at her bill from Schwartz and noticed charges for medical tests on her nervous system that he had never done.
He was indicted on 51 charges, including grand larceny. If convicted, he faces a possible 15-year prison sentence.
The doctor surrendered to authorities Thursday and was released on $35,000 bail.
His attorney, Stephen Scaring, said the doctor, who had been under investigation for two years, pleaded not guilty. "We're pleased that we can finally prove his innocence," he said.

Schwartz allegedly bilked more than $950,000 from Medicare, the federal care assistance programme for the elderly, and more than $120,000 from Medicaid, a federal programme that helps pay health care for the needy.
